146.input: A fixed capacity and an ordered stream of get(key) and put(key, value) calls.
atoms: Remove one node from an order
Insert one node at the most-recent end

operations.decision: Hash map from key to node
Keep LRU next to a tail sentinel

combine: The map owns key-to-node lookup; the list owns recency order.
Sentinel head and tail nodes remove empty/end special cases.
Every live key appears once in both structures.
solution: On get, locate the node; if absent return the miss value, otherwise move it to MRU and return it.
On put, update and move an existing node, or create a new MRU node.
After insertion, if size exceeds capacity, detach the LRU node and erase its map entry.

460.input: A capacity and get/put calls where eviction chooses minimum frequency, then least recency among ties.
atoms: Evict the oldest key in the minimum group
combine: Each entry stores value, frequency, and its list node.
Each frequency bucket is an LRU list.
minFrequency points to the only bucket eligible for eviction.
solution: A successful get or update removes the key from frequency f and inserts it as MRU in f+1.
If the old minimum bucket becomes empty, increment minFrequency.
A new key starts in frequency 1; when full, evict the LRU node from minFrequency first.

588.input: Absolute paths plus ls, mkdir, append-file, and read-file commands over an in-memory hierarchy.

operations.naive: Search a flat list of full paths

operations.decision: Sort child keys on demand or use ordered map
Store content on the terminal node

combine: A node has children, a file flag, and content; directories ignore content.
One path parser feeds every public operation.
Traversal can run in lookup-only or create-missing mode.
solution: Normalize the path into non-empty segments and walk from root.
mkdir creates directory nodes; addContent creates/marks the terminal file and appends.
ls returns the file name for a file path, otherwise sorted child names; read returns terminal content.
complexity: traversal: O(number of path segments) average
ls directory: O(c log c) for c children when sorting on demand

604.input: A run-length encoded string and repeated next()/hasNext() iterator calls.

operations.decision: Keep a cursor into encoded input

operations.target: O(digits parsed) only when a run starts

operations.decision: Check remaining count or unread input

combine: State is encoded cursor, current character, and remaining repetitions.
Parsing and emitting are separate smallest operations.
A run is parsed exactly once and never materialized.
solution: When remaining is zero, parse the next character and its entire decimal count.
next returns the current character and decrements remaining; return the specified sentinel if exhausted.
hasNext tests whether remaining output or unread encoded input exists.

1756.input: An initial queue 1..n and fetch(k) calls that remove the k-th item and append it to the MRU end.
atoms: Append one value at a new position
Preserve relative order of all other live values

operations.decision: Add -1 at the old Fenwick index

combine: An array maps physical position to value.
The Fenwick tree says which physical positions are still live.
Binary lifting/prefix search converts logical rank k into a physical position.
solution: Initialize positions 1..n with live count 1.
For fetch(k), find the smallest position whose prefix live count reaches k.
Remove that position, copy its value to the next unused tail position, mark the tail live, and return the value.

346.input: A window size and a stream of next(value) calls returning the average of the latest values.

operations.naive: Sum the window on every call: O(k)

operations.decision: Pop queue front when size exceeds k

combine: The queue is authoritative for membership; the sum is a derived index.
Every insertion updates both before any average is returned.
Every expired value is subtracted exactly once.
solution: Push the new value and add it to sum.
If queue size exceeds the configured window, pop front and subtract it.
Return sum divided by current queue size.

359.input: Chronological (timestamp, message) requests asking whether the message may print under a cooldown.
atoms: Compare current time with next allowed time

operations.naive: Count all occurrences in a window

operations.decision: Update only on an allowed print

combine: Each message is an independent tiny state machine.
Missing state means immediately allowed.
The stored time is the next legal timestamp, not merely the last request.
solution: Look up nextAllowed for the message.
If current time is earlier, return false without mutation.
Otherwise store current+cooldown and return true.

362.input: Chronological hit(timestamp) and getHits(timestamp) calls for a fixed recent-time window.
combine: Chronological input guarantees expired buckets form a prefix.
Equal timestamps share a bucket to handle high hit volume.
Deque membership and running total must change together.
solution: Before or during each operation, pop buckets older than the inclusive window and subtract their counts.
hit increments the last bucket if timestamps match, otherwise appends a new bucket; increment total.
getHits cleans then returns total.

933.input: Strictly increasing ping times; each ping returns how many fall in the latest 3000-time-unit interval.
atoms: Compare oldest time with lower bound

operations.decision: Append to queue because input is increasing

combine: The queue contains exactly the current valid interval.
Monotonic input makes every expired element appear at the front.
Each timestamp enters and leaves once.
solution: Append t.
Pop front while it is smaller than t-3000; keep the inclusive boundary.
Return queue length.
complexity: space: O(pings in the active window)

2034.input: Out-of-order update(timestamp, price) calls, including corrections, plus current/minimum/maximum queries.
atoms: Find old price for a timestamp
combine: The timestamp map is the source of truth.
The multiset is a derived view and must erase exactly one old occurrence on correction.
latestTimestamp changes only when a greater timestamp arrives.
solution: On update, if timestamp exists, erase one copy of its old price from the multiset.
Write the new map value, insert the new price, and maximize latestTimestamp.
current reads map[latestTimestamp]; minimum/maximum read the two multiset ends.

622.input: Capacity k and queue operations enQueue, deQueue, Front, Rear, isEmpty, and isFull.
combine: State is array, capacity, front index, and count.
Insertion index is (front+count) mod k.
Rear index is (front+count-1) mod k when non-empty.
solution: Reject enqueue when count==k; otherwise write at the computed insertion index and increment count.
Reject dequeue when count==0; otherwise advance front and decrement count.
Front/Rear read derived indices; empty/full compare count.

705.input: Integer keys with add, remove, and contains, without a built-in hash-table library.

operations.decision: Scan only the selected short chain

combine: The hash function chooses a bucket; equality chooses the exact key.
Buckets can be lists or small dynamic arrays.
Duplicate add and absent remove are no-ops.
solution: Compute a non-negative bucket index.
contains searches that bucket only.
add appends when absent; remove deletes the matching bucket entry.

706.input: Integer key/value pairs with put, get, and remove, without a built-in hash map.
atoms: Find matching entry in a bucket
combine: Hash narrows candidates; key equality resolves collisions.
Each bucket stores key/value entries, not values alone.
The missing-key return contract stays separate from stored values.
solution: Compute the bucket index from key.
put replaces a matching entry or inserts a new one.
get returns the matched value or missing sentinel; remove deletes only the matched key.

380.input: insert(value), remove(value), and uniform getRandom() with average O(1) requirements.
combine: The array provides density and random indexing.
The map provides direct membership and location.
After a swap, update the moved value's map index before popping.
solution: insert rejects existing values, otherwise maps value to array length and appends.
remove finds index, moves the last value into it, repairs that map entry, pops, and erases removed value.
getRandom samples an integer index uniformly from the array.

1206.input: search(target), add(number), and erase(number) over a sorted multiset-like structure without libraries.
atoms: Walk right while next is smaller

operations.decision: Reuse predecessors and bypass one tower

combine: Level 0 contains all values; higher levels contain random subsets.
A sentinel head owns the maximum number of forward pointers.
One top-down walk records the update point at every level.
solution: Search moves right then down until level 0.
Add samples a geometric height and splices a new tower after recorded predecessors.
Erase records predecessors, verifies a matching level-0 node, and bypasses it at every level where present.

1603.input: Initial counts for three parking-space types and addCar(type) commands.
atoms: Map car type to one counter

operations.naive: Allocate then roll back on failure

combine: Each car type is independent state.
The remaining counter is the only source of truth.
A failed addCar cannot change any counter.
solution: Translate 1-based carType to the matching array index.
If remaining is zero, return false.
Otherwise decrement once and return true.

1396.input: checkIn(id, station, time), checkOut(id, station, time), and average queries for directed station pairs.
combine: Active trips are transient; route aggregates are historical.
Checkout is the transaction that removes active state and updates one route.
Routes are directed, so (A,B) differs from (B,A).
solution: checkIn writes active[id].
checkOut reads/removes active[id], builds the route key, and adds elapsed time plus one count.
getAverageTime returns total/count for that route.

1797.input: A TTL and strictly increasing generate, renew, and count-unexpired calls for token IDs.

operations.decision: Lazy validation against current map expiry

combine: The map is authoritative; the queue is only a chronological cleanup index.
Generate/renew append a new expiry event.
When popping, delete a token only if the event expiry still equals its current mapped expiry.
solution: Clean events with expiry <= current time.
generate stores current+TTL and enqueues it.
renew succeeds only for a mapped unexpired token, then writes/enqueues a new expiry; count cleans and returns map size.
complexity: space: O(tokens + renewal events not yet cleaned)

2043.input: Initial account balances and transfer, deposit, and withdraw commands with 1-based account numbers.

operations.decision: Debit and credit only after both accounts/funds pass

combine: The balance array is the source of truth.
A command has a validation phase and a commit phase.
Use a wide integer type for accumulated balances.
solution: Centralize account validity.
Deposit validates then adds; withdraw validates account and funds then subtracts.
Transfer validates both accounts and source funds, then applies debit and credit together.

2241.input: Deposits of five denomination counts and withdrawals that must greedily prefer larger banknotes.
atoms: Choose usable notes from largest downward
combine: Inventory is five counts aligned with denomination values.
The greedy rule is a business requirement, not a claim of general coin-system optimality.
Planning and mutation are separate phases.
solution: deposit adds each provided count.
withdraw scans denominations high to low, records chosen notes, and reduces a local remaining amount.
If remaining is nonzero return failure; otherwise subtract the planned counts and return them.

355.input: postTweet, follow, unfollow, and getNewsFeed calls; feeds return the newest ten relevant tweets.

operations.naive: Insert into one globally sorted list
operations.decision: Append to per-user tweet list with global sequence
Hash set of followees per user
Max-heap k-way merge of list tails

combine: Per-user lists are append-only and already recency-sorted.
The social graph selects which lists participate.
Heap entries carry author and index so the next older tweet from that author can be added.
solution: post appends (sequence,tweetId) to the user's list.
follow/unfollow update the set while self-posts are always considered.
Feed seeds one latest tweet per relevant author, repeatedly pops newest and pushes that author's predecessor until ten or empty.

1500.input: An initial chunk count plus join(ownedChunks), leave(user), and request(user, chunk) operations with reusable smallest user IDs.

operations.decision: Min-heap of recycled IDs plus nextId

combine: Ownership is indexed in both directions and both views must agree.
A request snapshots existing owners before adding the requester.
Leaving removes every reverse edge, erases the user, and recycles the ID.
solution: join chooses heap minimum or nextId, stores the user's chunk set, and inserts the user into each owner set.
request returns the ordered owners; when non-empty, add the chunk to requester and requester to owners.
leave iterates that user's chunks to erase reverse ownership, then pushes the ID into the free heap.
complexity: join/leave: proportional to owned chunks with set costs
request: O(number of owners + log owners)

1912.input: Shop/movie/price inventory and search(movie), rent(shop,movie), drop(shop,movie), report() operations with precise ordering and top-five limits.
atoms: Find cheapest available copies for one movie
combine: The price map is canonical immutable metadata.
Availability and rented sets are mutually exclusive materialized views.
Tuple ordering exactly encodes every tie-break rule.
solution: Initialize prices and insert every copy into its movie's available set.
search iterates the first five available tuples.
rent erases available and inserts rented; drop reverses it; report iterates the first five global rented tuples.

2296.input: Text-editor commands addText, deleteText, cursorLeft, and cursorRight, with short context returned around the cursor.
atoms: Read up to ten characters left of cursor

operations.naive: Edit middle of one string: O(n)

operations.decision: Transfer chars between left and right stacks/buffers

combine: Left buffer is text before cursor in normal order.
Right buffer stores text after cursor in a representation that makes its near end cheap.
The complete document is left + reverse(right) when stacks are used.
solution: add appends to left; delete removes min(k,left size) from left.
cursorLeft moves characters from left to right; cursorRight moves them back.
After delete or movement, return the last up-to-ten characters of left.

3484.input: A fixed-row, 26-column sheet with setCell, resetCell, and evaluation of formulas containing two operands joined by plus.
atoms: Classify operand as literal or cell

operations.decision: Parse the single '+' and resolve two tokens

combine: Unset cells and reset cells both resolve to zero.
One resolve(token) helper handles literals and addresses.
Storage and parsing remain independent so the supported grammar is explicit.
solution: set writes the cell key; reset erases it.
getValue removes the leading '=', splits once at '+', and resolves both operands.
A token beginning with a letter reads the map with default zero; otherwise parse the integer; return their sum.

432.input: inc(key), dec(key), getMaxKey(), and getMinKey() with every operation required in O(1) average time.
atoms: Find a key's current count group
Choose any key in a group

operations.decision: Doubly linked list of existing count buckets

operations.naive: One node per key breaks adjacency

combine: Buckets are strictly ordered by count but only existing counts are stored.
The key map points directly to the containing bucket.
Empty buckets are removed immediately so the two ends always represent min and max.
solution: inc moves a key to count+1, creating the adjacent bucket when absent; a new key enters count 1.
dec moves to count-1 or deletes a count-1 key.
After every move remove an empty old bucket; min/max return any key from the first/last real bucket.
